standing_words.engine: the block only arranges what the engine laws it cites require; it carries no balance value
standing_words.shipped: the block repeats a shape that shipped content already uses; exemplars name it
standing_words.proposed: the block rests on a value the director has not ratified; compile says so every time it is used

_meta.purpose: Named behaviours. Each builder in scripts/library.py returns AI rules made through the build skill's factory.py. An entry adds no number: every number is a parameter the sheet supplies, or a pool record's own gate.

rule_pattern/use_jutsu/v1.summary: Use one pool jutsu when it is in reach.
failure_modes: A gate other than range + 1 fires out of range or forfeits the outer band (law 40); the builder takes the gate from the pool record, so it cannot be set here.
A ground-target jutsu is refused: it belongs to the boss fight grammar.

rule_pattern/rotation/v1.summary: Use each listed pool jutsu in priority order; the engine's cooldowns make the order a rotation.
failure_modes: Rules are tried top to bottom and the first that can act wins, so the order is the priority (law 39).
Two jutsu that share a cooldown group lock each other out (law 91); the group table is live data and is not checked here.

rule_pattern/opener/v1.summary: Use a self-target stance first, before any attack.
exemplars: building-tnr-content/references/lines.md (the Verge line kits open on a stance)
failure_modes: A stealth stance as the opener stops the AI attacking that round (law 62); the builder refuses it.
With no 40 AP action the AI cannot fill a 100 AP turn (laws 61, 63).

rule_pattern/basic_attack/v1.summary: Use the engine's basic attack on an adjacent opponent.
failure_modes: It needs no kit entry; adding a pool code for it is a mistake.

rule_pattern/fallback/v1.summary: The unconditional last rule: close distance, or strike then close, or end the turn.
failure_modes: A list with no unconditional last rule lets the AI fall off the end (law 41); compile adds this block when a sheet leaves it out, and says so.
It takes no `when`: a conditional last rule is not a last rule.
